# search_catalog_results fixtures

Each file here is a real `search_catalog` tool call output (the `<search_results>...</search_results>`
string produced by `format_search_results()` in `api/assistant/agent.py`), captured from a live
`/chat` request. They're used to stub `search_catalog` (see `stub_function_tool()` in
`tests/factories.py`) so tests can exercise the agent/result-reason behavior against realistic
catalog data without depending on the search index or making a real search call.

## Naming convention

`<query-with-dashes-instead-of-spaces>-search_catalog-result-<date-generated>.txt`

e.g. `Hayao-Miyazaki-search_catalog-result-2026-04-14.txt` was generated by searching
`Hayao Miyazaki`.

## Generating a new fixture / updating an existing one

1. Start the local API server pointed at an environment with real catalog data. See the main
   [README](../../../README.md#run-locally) "Start localhost server" step.

2. Run `scripts/gen_search_catalog_fixture.py`, which makes a `/chat` catalogSearch request and
   writes the search tool's raw output straight into this directory, named per the convention
   above (pass `--outdir` to write elsewhere):

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=. uv run python scripts/gen_search_catalog_fixture.py "<query>"
   ```

3. Update the query -> fixture filename mapping wherever the fixture is used (e.g.
   `tests/stochastic_processes/test_agent_responses.py`) if you changed the filename.

## Notes

- Real search results change over time as the catalog/index changes, so regenerating a fixture
  for the same query can produce a different set of editions/barcodes. Check that any test
  asserting on specific fixture content (e.g. a specific title or barcode) still holds after
  regenerating.
